subject: 🎯 Stock Finder: Sun Oct 4 shortlist | AI-infra breakouts lead, SMTC best setup
html_body:
Stock Finder — Momentum Discovery

Sunday, October 4, 2026 — Kuwait time

7 candidates cleared all gates

AI-infrastructure theme dominates this scan (semis, optics, AI cloud). Two loud web-search stories — Accenture's "21% earnings pop" and Astera Labs' analyst-target chase — turned out to be stale or already reversed once checked against live IBKR data. Best actionable setup: SMTC.

How this run went

~35 raw tickers surfaced across 25+ web searches. 11 were checked against live IBKR quotes and price history; 4 failed on sight (haram/defense/too speculative to bother checking). 7 cleared all 4 gates. No small-cap survived this run (ETON was the only one in contention and it was dropped — see below) — today's board skews mid/large-cap. That's a real finding, not padding: 4 large-cap, 3 mid-cap, 0 small-cap.

Sizing caveat: today's daily-check email flagged your cash balance as unconfirmed (portfolio.json shows $330.60, but a Sept 29 IBKR pull showed $432.16, and CLAUDE.md's last snapshot shows $546.58). Order-plan share counts below use $432 (the most recent IBKR-sourced figure) as the 15% base ≈ $65/position — re-run the math once the cash figure is reconciled.

🎯 Momentum Shortlist

Run analyze [TICKER] on any name for the full deep dive before sizing a real order.
#1 — SMTC Semtech Corp ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

SEMICONDUCTORS MID CAP

Signal: Broke out to a new 52-week high ($201.99) Friday Oct 2 on heavy volume (2.9M shares) — Oppenheimer raised its target to $225 (from $200) and Baird to $300 (from $225) on Oct 1, citing AI data-center demand (projected >40% of revenue) plus a new robot-chip product. Pulled back intraday to close at $194.88, a day ago.

Price: $194.90 (IBKR live) | Volume: ~2.9M shares Friday (well above the ~2M daily average) | RS vs SPY: stock +44% over 1 month vs a flat broad market — clear outperformance.

Why it's interesting: This is the cleanest setup in the scan — a fresh breakout with two separate sell-side target hikes landing the same week, and analyst targets ($225–$300) sit well above the current price, meaning the "room to run" isn't just chart space, it's consensus-backed.

Realistic near-term target: +10–15% over 5–10 trading days — toward the $215–$225 analyst-target cluster.

Entry read: BUY AT MARKET — already pulled back from Friday's exact high within the same session; not chasing a vertical candle.

Order plan (GTC): BUY limit $195.50 · stop-limit trigger $185.00 / limit $183.50 (below Thursday's close and the breakout base) · TP1 sell limit $215.00 · TP2 $225.00 · size ~0.33 sh ≈ $65 (~15% of $432) · R:R ~1.6:1 to TP1, ~2.5:1 to TP2

Event window: No dated event risk ahead — earnings already behind it. ✅

Halal: ✅ Verified — semiconductor component manufacturer, core business clean.

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear — catalyst is AI/data-center demand, not a government contract.

Sizing note: requires fractional shares (confirm enabled). Commission drag ~3.1% of a $65 position — TP1's +10% clears it easily.

Next step: analyze SMTC
#2 — NBIS Nebius Group NV ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

AI CLOUD INFRA LARGE CAP

Signal: Jumped on Oct 1 after announcing higher on-demand GPU/CPU/memory pricing (pricing power) plus the Inferize acquisition for its AI inference stack — continued higher into Friday's close ($242.81, +4.6% on the day). 2 trading days ago.

Price: $242.98 (IBKR live) | Volume: ~12.3M shares | RS vs SPY: outperforming sharply — company reports 454% YoY revenue growth.

Why it's interesting: A pricing-power story is a different (and arguably healthier) catalyst than a one-time earnings pop — it signals demand outstripping supply. Still ~13% below its 13-week high of $280.83, so there's real room before the next resistance.

Realistic near-term target: +5–11% over 5–10 trading days — toward the $255–$270 zone below the 13-week high.

Entry read: BUY AT MARKET — not extended relative to its own recent range.

Order plan (GTC): BUY limit $243.00 · stop-limit trigger $230.00 / limit $228.00 (below Thursday's low) · TP1 sell limit $255.00 · TP2 $270.00 · size ~0.27 sh ≈ $65 (~15% of $432) · R:R ~0.8:1 to TP1, ~1.8:1 to TP2

Event window: No dated event behind this — pure flow/pricing catalyst. ✅

Halal: ✅ Verified — AI cloud computing infrastructure provider.

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear. Note: Nebius is a "preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner" for some of Palantir's customers — Nebius itself isn't a defense contractor and today's catalyst is the GPU pricing news, not that partnership, so it doesn't trip the exclusion, but flagging for your own comfort level.

Sizing note: requires fractional shares (confirm enabled).

Next step: analyze NBIS
#3 — AAOI Applied Optoelectronics ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

AI DATA CENTER OPTICS MID CAP

Signal: New 800G hyperscale AI order news drove two straight up days: +8.1% Thursday Oct 1, +7.7% Friday Oct 2 (close $115.59) on heavy volume (~17–20M shares both days). 1–2 trading days ago, signal still intact.

Price: $115.01 (IBKR live) | Volume: ~17-20M shares/day this week | RS vs SPY: strongly outperforming (+231% YTD per company reporting, though see caution below).

Why it's interesting: A real, named catalyst (hyperscale order) with two days of confirming volume. Caution: this name's 52-week high is $233.67 — more than double today's price — meaning it already had a violent boom-bust cycle this year (52-week low $18.50). It's not "extended vs. its own history," but the volatility profile is high; this +16.5% 2-day move itself is a short-term extension that argues for a pullback entry, not a chase.

Realistic near-term target: +10–19% over 5–10 trading days if the pullback holds.

Entry read: WAIT FOR PULLBACK to $108–$110 — don't chase the 2-day spike.

Order plan (GTC, if filled near $109): BUY limit $109.00 · stop-limit trigger $107.00 / limit $105.50 (below Thursday's close) · TP1 sell limit $120.00 · TP2 $130.00 · size ~0.60 sh ≈ $65 (~15% of $432) · R:R ~3.1:1 to TP1, ~6:1 to TP2

Event window: No dated event risk ahead — already a reaction to news, not a bet on one. ✅

Halal: ✅ Verified — optical components manufacturer for telecom/data centers.

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear — catalyst is a commercial hyperscaler order, not a government contract.

Sizing note: high historical volatility (round-tripped from $18.50 to $233.67 and back this past year) — this is the riskiest name on the list; size conservatively even within the 15% cap.

Next step: analyze AAOI
#4 — HPE Hewlett Packard Enterprise ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

ENTERPRISE TECH / NETWORKING LARGE CAP

Signal: Jumped +7.9% Friday Oct 2 to a brand-new 52-week high ($70.29) on AI-networking demand; multiple analysts (Truist, Piper Sandler, Wells Fargo) have raised targets this week. 1 trading day ago.

Price: $69.67 (IBKR live) | Volume: ~29M shares, far above average | RS vs SPY: clearly leading.

Why it's interesting: This is the single freshest, strongest % move in the whole scan — but it's also now sitting just 0.9% below its own 52-week high with almost no room left before it needs to make a new high to keep going.

Realistic near-term target: +7–12% over 5–10 trading days, contingent on a pullback entry.

Entry read: WAIT FOR PULLBACK to $66.50–$67.50 — chasing a stock 0.9% off its all-time high the day after a 7.9% pop is exactly the kind of entry that got ACN burned this week (see Cut list below).

Order plan (GTC, if filled near $67): BUY limit $67.00 · stop-limit trigger $65.00 / limit $64.50 (below the breakout day's own low) · TP1 sell limit $72.00 · TP2 $75.00 · size ~0.97 sh ≈ $65 (~15% of $432) · R:R ~2:1 to TP1, ~3.2:1 to TP2

Event window: Earnings already behind it. ✅

Halal: ✅ Verified — enterprise servers/networking hardware and software.

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear — HPE has federal IT customers but is not a defense prime, and today's catalyst is commercial AI-networking demand, not a contract award.

Sizing note: none — priced for whole or fractional shares either way.

Next step: analyze HPE
#5 — GME GameStop Corp ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

CONSUMER RETAIL LARGE CAP

Signal: CEO/Chairman Ryan Cohen bought 700,000 shares on Oct 2 (fresh Form 4) — stock closed up 4.4% that session near its 52-week high. 1-2 trading days ago.

Price: $25.16 (IBKR live) | Volume: ~13.5M shares | RS vs SPY: outperforming, near highs.

Why it's interesting: An insider buy this size, by the Chairman himself, is one of the cleanest "smart money" signals this scan produced. The catch: only 6.4% room to the 52-week high ($26.87) before the stock needs a fresh catalyst to keep climbing, so near-term upside is capped unless it breaks out.

Realistic near-term target: +5–9% over 5–10 trading days, capped below a 52-week-high breakout.

Entry read: BUY AT MARKET (small size) — the insider signal justifies a position, but don't oversize given the capped near-term R:R.

Order plan (GTC): BUY limit $25.20 · stop-limit trigger $23.80 / limit $23.50 (below this week's base) · TP1 sell limit $26.50 · TP2 $27.50 (above 52w high) · size ~2 sh ≈ $50.40 (~12% of $432) · R:R ~0.8:1 to TP1, ~1.4:1 to TP2 — weakest R:R on this list, flagged accordingly.

Event window: No dated event. ✅

Halal: ✅ Verified — video game and consumer electronics retailer (business-activity screen; no alcohol/gambling/weapons in the core business).

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear.

Sizing note: cheap enough for whole shares — no fractional needed.

Next step: analyze GME
#6 — VIAV Viavi Solutions ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

NETWORK TEST EQUIPMENT MID CAP

Signal: Unusual call option activity (10x average volume, concentrated at the $40/$46 Oct 16 strikes) coincided with a 2-day, +12.4% price run: +6.8% Thu Oct 1, +5.2% Fri Oct 2 (close $47.10). 1-2 trading days ago.

Price: $47.10 (IBKR live) | Volume: ~10M shares | RS vs SPY: outperforming, at a 13-week high.

Why it's interesting: Options flow leading price is a classic smart-money tell. But the stock is now only 2.8% below its 13-week high ($48.42) — minimal room before it needs new highs to justify a chase.

Realistic near-term target: +7–16% over 5–10 trading days if the pullback holds and it clears the recent high.

Entry read: WAIT FOR PULLBACK to $44.50–$45.00.

Order plan (GTC, if filled near $44.75): BUY limit $44.75 · stop-limit trigger $43.50 / limit $43.00 · TP1 sell limit $48.00 · TP2 $52.00 (near the options strike zone) · size ~1.45 sh ≈ $65 (~15% of $432) · R:R ~1.9:1 to TP1, ~4.1:1 to TP2

Event window: No dated event; options expiry Oct 16 is a flow factor to watch, not a binary bet. ✅

Halal: ✅ Verified — network/telecom test & measurement equipment maker. Minor note: Viavi has a small optical-security (anti-counterfeiting currency features) segment — non-weapons, not a primary business line.

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear — not a defense contractor; today's catalyst is options flow, not a contract.

Sizing note: requires fractional shares (confirm enabled).

Next step: analyze VIAV
#7 — CRWD CrowdStrike Holdings ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)

CYBERSECURITY SOFTWARE LARGE CAP

Signal: Grinding to new 52-week highs all week on AI-driven cybersecurity demand; TD Cowen raised its target to $280 on Oct 2. Closed Friday at $270.04, a new high. 1 trading day ago.

Price: $269.90 (IBKR live) | Volume: ~5.9M shares | RS vs SPY: clear leader, steady uptrend for 3+ weeks.

Why it's interesting: The most mainstream, most-covered name on this list — real strength, but it's also the one everyone already sees, and it's sitting just 1.3% below its all-time high with almost no cushion.

Realistic near-term target: +5–9% over 5–10 trading days, contingent on a pullback.

Entry read: WAIT FOR PULLBACK to $260–$263 — weakest risk/reward on this list if bought at market.

Order plan (GTC, if filled near $261): BUY limit $261.00 · stop-limit trigger $258.00 / limit $256.00 (below Thursday's low) · TP1 sell limit $275.00 · TP2 $285.00 · size ~0.25 sh ≈ $65 (~15% of $432) · R:R ~2.8:1 to TP1, ~4.8:1 to TP2

Event window: No dated event behind it. ✅

Halal: ✅ Verified — cybersecurity software.

Defense/military check: ✅ Clear — serves government cybersecurity clients but is not a defense/munitions contractor, and the catalyst is commercial AI demand, not a contract award.

Sizing note: requires fractional shares (confirm enabled).

Next step: analyze CRWD

Cut this run — show the work

ACN (Accenture) — search reported a +21% post-earnings "best day ever" surge, but live IBKR data shows that move already reversed: down 6.0% in the most recent session, from $212.30 to $199.51. Classic faded-narrative trap — dropped.
ALAB (Astera Labs) — four analysts raised price targets this week (Citi $430, Roth $450, RBC $500), but the stock itself closed down 1.7% on the day with no fresh bullish print. Target chatter isn't a live signal — dropped.
OKLO — search called it a nuclear momentum name, but IBKR shows it's 79% below its 52-week high and still sliding despite positive business news (Meta power deal, DOE pairing). Stale/bearish — dropped.
SOUN (SoundHound AI) — flagged as a short-squeeze setup, but actual news flow this week is negative: shareholder-litigation probe, a Piper Sandler downgrade, and insider-sale filings. Fails the "live momentum" gate — dropped.
ASPN (Aspen Aerogels) — beat revenue estimates, but shares are still down ~50% over the past month on a dilutive equity raise and EV-demand concerns. Conflicted signal — dropped.
VICR (Vicor) — the "raised guidance, +12%" story looks stale; today's actual move is a flat +0.8%. No fresh confirmation — dropped.
ETON (Eton Pharmaceuticals) — search described a clean "+51% since earnings" continuation, but the price history shows an unexplained ~14% crash on Sep 30 before a partial bounce. Too choppy to call a clean setup — dropped rather than pass through a narrative the chart doesn't support.
MRK (Merck) — a Dow-leaderboard headline exists, but today's IBKR move is flat (+0.2%); likely already priced in — dropped.
CPRI (Capri Holdings) — no live catalyst this week; the one recent news item is a routine executive appointment, and earnings aren't until Nov 3 — fails freshness — dropped.
TER (Teradyne), APLD (Applied Digital) — IBKR returned stale/empty snapshots with no volume or change data; couldn't confirm either is moving right now, so both were dropped rather than guessed at.
RKLB (Rocket Lab) — excluded on sight: a space-launch provider with substantial national-security/DoD launch contracts falls under the defense exclusion even though it isn't a classic "prime."
ECPG (Encore Capital Group) — excluded on sight: core business is buying and collecting charged-off consumer debt — interest-based finance, fails the halal screen.
AMOD, SDEV, AIXI — speculative microcap pops (8-K-driven spikes, no durable catalyst) — too thin/pump-risk to spend an IBKR check on.

🏆 Today's Best Setup

SMTC — Semtech Corp

Fresh breakout to a new 52-week high, backed by two separate analyst target hikes landing the same week (Oppenheimer → $225, Baird → $300) — both well above today's $194.90, so the upside case is consensus-backed, not just chart extrapolation. It's also the only name on this list that's actionable at market right now without waiting for a pullback, since Friday's own session already pulled back from the exact high before closing.

Invalidation: a close back below $183.50 — that's beneath both Thursday's close and the base the breakout launched from. Below that, the breakout thesis is wrong; this is the stop reference, not a percentage guess.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results. All prices and order plans are derived from live IBKR quotes and daily price history as of Friday Oct 2, 2026 close (markets closed over the weekend) — re-verify prices Monday before placing any order. Halal screening is business-activity only per your standing definition; re-verify quarterly on Zoya or Musaffa if your definition changes. Generated Sunday, October 4, 2026, Kuwait time.
